newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-taking clips Bombay shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking clips Bombay shares at close.

text.p: ** (1000 GMT) Bombay shares finish in negative territory
** Benchmark Bombay index closes 27.76 points, or 0.63 percent, lower at provisional 4,376.93 -- off 4,448.06 morning high
** Business squaring deals stall rally ahead of weekly close of accounts on Friday-traders
** National exchange index ends 3.15 points off at provisional 1,235.75
Late profit-taking dragged Bombay shares down at close on Thursday as the market failed to make progress after starting strongly, brokers said.
"The market was pulled down in the last 15 minutes," said Dinesh Valji at brokerage Valji Bhimji & Company.
Friday is the last day of the weekly settlement on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
The 30-share BSE index fell 27.76 points, or 0.63 percent, to 4,376.93 provisional close after ralling to a new 33-month high of 4,448.06 in morning trade.
Analysts saw the setback as a temporary correction before the market gathered momentum.
"I do expect the market to cross the all-time highs in the next 15 days," said Ashith Kampani at brokerage JSB Securities Ltd. "There's lot of money and equities appear to be best bet."
Falling interest rates have made fixed income instruments less attractive, he said.
The BSE index punched through the 4,400-point barrier on Wednesday for the first time since mid-October 1994, and traders expect an assault on the all-time peak of 4,643.31 set on September 12, 1994.
Foreign funds had been the chief buyers behind the surge and analysts see local institutions like the Unit Trust of India (UTI) to step their purchases.
"I expect the UTI to pump in money," Kampani said.
UTI, India's largest mutual fund, is currently raising funds through sale of units at the beginning of its financial year which began on July 1.
UTI expects to raise 120-150 billion rupees in 1997/98.
